content:
nora: FYI, found a parity/behavior mismatch in batch embeddings that broke the sample-app onboarding tests for private clusters. REST returns 207 Multi-Status with per-item errors, but python SDK v1.6.0 coalesces to 200 and silences item errors. Users saw missing vectors and no error.
david: Ouch. Can you paste the curl and sdk calls?
nora: curl I used (proxying to private shim):
```
curl -i -X POST https://private.api.redwood.local/v1/embeddings:batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-batch","inputs":["good","bad","maybe"],"return_errors":true}'
```
This returns HTTP/1.1 207 Multi-Status and body like:
```
[
  {"index":0,"status":200,"vector":[0.1,0.2,...]},
  {"index":1,"status":400,"error":"invalid input"},
  {"index":2,"status":200,"vector":[0.3,0.4,...]}
]
```
But python SDK call:
```python
resp = client.embeddings.batch_create(inputs=['good','bad','maybe'], model='embed-batch', return_errors=True)
print(resp.vectors)
# prints only two vectors, no indication of the failed item; resp.status_code == 200
```
I also captured the raw HTTP request from the SDK via a proxy: it sent `{"model":"embed-batch","inputs":[...],"returnErrors":true}` (camelCased) which the private service treats as unknown and falls back to default `return_errors=false`.
priya: So two separate drifts: field-name normalization and HTTP status handling. Additionally, our rate-limit headers differ in private: infra emits `Retry-After-ms` (ms) and the SDK expects `Retry-After` seconds. SDK parses the value as seconds, so it retries much sooner and triggers repeated 429s.
sre: We got reports of a retry storm in the private shim overnight. Logs show: 429 -> SDK reads Retry-After "12000" -> treated as 12000s? or sometimes 12s depending on parsing path -> inconsistent behavior. We should standardize on Retry-After seconds header and/or have SDK support ms header.
david: Action items I propose: 1) SDK should preserve snake_case field names for server-critical endpoints or allow callers to pass `raw_body` when they need exact control (I'll own a small patch). 2) SDK must not coalesce 207 Multi-Status to 200; instead surface per-item statuses in the response object and raise a PartialSuccess error when any item failed. 3) SDK retry logic: honor both `Retry-After` (secs) and `Retry-After-ms` (ms) and prefer server header semantics. 4) Update sample-app quickstart to show handling partial responses.
priya: I'll update the sample-app to call `batch_create(..., raw_body={...})` as a temporary workaround and add a section about checking per-item statuses. Also adding a short note in the onboarding doc about private vs public strictness.
sre: I'll add a compatibility shim in private to emit `Retry-After` (secs) for now and file infra issue to normalise headers.
alice-qa: I'll add nightly regression that runs curl vs SDK for the batch embeddings flow and asserts per-item parity. I'll also add a test for Retry-After parsing to prevent future regressions.
devex-bot: Created issues: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/9800 (preserve snake_case + partial success surfacing) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/9801 (standardise Retry-After header in private). Assigned to david and sre respectively.
nora: Thanks. One last nit: please make sure SDK error object includes index and original message so app owners can handle retries only for failed items. We've already had a customer re-ingest the whole batch because SDK didn't expose the failed index.
david: Good call. I'll include `PartialSuccessError.failed_indices` and `failed_reasons` in the PR. Expect draft today.
priya: I'll put a short snippet in the quickstart: `for i, item in enumerate(resp.items): if item.status != 200: handle_failure(i, item.error)` until SDK lands.
nora: Great, thanks everyone :)
